FOREWORD 


This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the Pesticides 
and Pesticides Residue Analysis Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Division 
Council. 


Acetamiprid, SP formulation is used in the control of insects in agricultural crops. 
Acetamiprid, SP is generally manufactured to contain 20 percent (m/m) of acetamiprid. 


In the formulation of this standard, due consideration has been given to the provisions of the Insecticides Act, 
1968 and the Rules framed thereunder. However, this standard is subject to the restrictions imposed under the 
Insecticides Act and Rules, wherever applicable. 


For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, 
observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 
‘Rules for rounding off numerical values (revised)’. The number of significant places retained in the rounded off 
value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard. 


IS 16328 : 2017 


Indian Standard 
ACETAMIPRID, SP — SPECIFICATION 


1 SCOPE 


This standard prescribes the requirements and the 
methods of sampling and test for Acetamiprid, SP. 


2 REFERENCES 


The following standards contain provisions which, 
through reference in this text, constitute provisions of 
this standard. At the time of publication, the editions 
indicated were valid. All standards are subject to 
revision, and parties to agreements based on this 
standard are encouraged to investigate the possibility 
of applying the most recent editions of the standards 
indicated below:

3 REQUIREMENTS 


3.1 Constituents 


3.1.1 The material shall consist of acetamiprid 
technical, together with suitable carrier(s), wetting 
agent(s), and colouring agent. 


3.1.2 Acetamiprid technical employed in the 
formulation of this material shall conform to IS 15981. 


3.2 Description 


The product shall be in the form of homogenous free 
flowing powder, free from any extraneous matter. 


3.3 The material shall comply with the requirements 
given in Table 1. 


3.3.1 Acetamiprid Content 


When determined by the method prescribed in Annex 
A, the observed acetamiprid content percent (m/m) of 


any of the samples shall not differ from the declared 
nominal value, by more than the percent tolerance 
limits indicated below: 


Nominal Value Tolerance Limits 
Percent Percent 
Up to 9 +10 
BE l 
Above 9 and below 50 +5 of the nominal 
value 
50 and above +5 
-3 
4 PACKING 


4.1 Primary Packing 


Products of 20g, 50g, 100g, 250g, 500g and 1 kg shall 
be packed in multilayer non-gusseted aluminium 
laminated flexograph pouch made from PET (12 vu 
aluminium foil (9 u)/LDPE (0.062 mm) and four-side 
heat-sealed. 


4.2 Secondary Packing 


Primary pack shall be individually inserted in 
cardboard carton, which shall be further packed in CFB 
boxes conforming to IS 2771 (Part 1). 


4.3 Transport Packing 


The capacity of the CFB containing primary packaging 
up to 500 g shall be 2.0 kg and those containing primary 
packaging of 1.0 kg shall be 5 kg. 


4.3.1 Bulk Transport Packing 


Product shall be packed in galvanized iron drums (see 
IS 2552) with LDPE liner of thickness 1.0 mm 
(capacity of 5kg, 10kg, 20kg, 25kg and 50kg). 


4.4 The packing shall also meet the general 
requirements given in IS 8190 (Part 1).

5 MARKING 


5.1 The containers shall be securely closed and the 
following information shall be marked legibly and 
indelibly on each container in addition to any other 
information, as is necessary under the Insecticides Act, 
1968 and Rules framed thereunder: 


a) Name of the material; 

b) Name and address of the manufacturer; 

c) Batch number; 

d) Date of manufacture; 

e) Date of expiry; 

f) Net quantity; 

g) Nominal acetamiprid content, percent (m/m); 

h) Cautionary notice worded as in the 
Insecticides Act, 1968 and Rules framed 
thereunder; and 

j) Any other information required under the 
Legal Metrology (Packaged Commodities) 
Rules, 2011. 


5.2 BIS Certification Marking 


The product may also be marked with the Standard 
Mark. 


5.2.1 The use of the Standard Mark is governed by 
the provisions of Bureau of Indian Standards Act, 1986 
and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The 
details of conditions under which the licence for the 


use of the Standard Mark may be granted to 
manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the 
Bureau of Indian Standards. 


6 SAMPLING 


When freshly manufactured material in bulk quantity 
and/or the retail pack of the formulated product is/are 
offered for inspection, representative sample of the 
material shall be drawn and tested as prescribed in 
IS 10627, and if tested within 90 days of its date of 
manufacture, the criteria for conformity shall be that 
the contents in percent (m/m), shall not be less than 
the declared nominal value. The upper limit for 
conformity shall be the same as those given in 3.3.1. 


When the material is offered for inspection after 
90 days of its manufacture, sampling shall be done as 
prescribed in IS 10627. However, the criteria for 
conformity of the material, when tested, shall be the 
limits of tolerances, as applicable over the declared 
nominal value, and given under 3.3.1. 


7 TESTS 

7.1 Tests shall be carried out by the methods referred 
to in col 4 of Table 1. 

7.2 Quality of Reagents 


Unless specified otherwise, pure chemicals and reagent 
grade water (see IS 1070) shall be employed in tests. 


NOTE — ‘Pure chemicals’ shall mean chemicals that do not 
contain impurities, which affect the results of analysis.

DETERMINATION OF ACETAMIPRID CONTENT 


A-1 PRINCIPLE 


The acetamiprid content is determined by high 
performance liquid chromatography (HPLC) equipped 
with UV-VIS detector using internal standard 
technique. 


A-2 APPARATUS 


A-2.1 A high performance liquid chromatography 
system equipped with ultraviolet detector and 
chromatographic software/printer plotter-cum- 
integrator or PC based data system is used for this 
determination. The suggested operative parameters are 
as follows, but can be changed if necessary, provided 
standardization is done: 


Column : Stainless steel, 25 cm x 4.6 


mm i.d., packed with C-18 of 
5 um particle size 

: Ambient 

: Acetonitrile, 30.0 ml 

: Water, 70.0 ml 
Ortho-phosphoric acid 
(85 percent w/w), 0.35 ml 

: 1.0 ml/min 


Temperature 
Mobile phase 


Flow rate 
Injection volume: 20 pl 


Detector : Ultraviolet detector (250 nm) 


A typical HPLC chromatogram of acetamiprid SP with 
internal standard is given in Fig. 1

A-3 REAGENTS 
A-3.1 Acetonitrile, HPLC/AR grade. 
A-3.2 Water, HPLC grade. 


A-3.3 Ortho-Phosphoric Acid, HPLC/AR grade, 
85 percent (w/w). 


A-3.4 4-Hydroxy Methyl Benzoate, internal 
standard, of known purity. 


A-3.5 Acetamiprid Reference Standard, of known 
purity. 


A-4 PROCEDURE 


A-4.1 Preparation of Internal Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately about 200 mg of 4-hydroxy methyl 
benzoate into a 100 ml beaker. Transfer the contents 
quantitatively, into a clean 250 ml volumetric flask by 
dissolving it in acetonitrile. Sonicate, and make up the 
volume upto the mark with acetonitrile. Shake well to 
homogenize. 


A-4.2 Preparation of Standard Solution 


Weigh accurately about 80 mg of acetamiprid reference 
standard into a 100 ml volumetric flask. Add about 
50 ml of acetonitrile. Sonicate, and make up the volume 


up to the mark with acetonitrile. Pipette out 10 ml of 
above stock solution into a 100 ml volumetric flask. 
Add 10 ml of the internal standard solution to it. Make 
up the volume upto the mark with mobile phase. Shake 
well to homogenize. 


A-4.3 Preparation of Sample Solution 


Weigh out accurately (to the nearest 1 mg), quantity 
of sample so as to contain 80 mg of the active ingredient 
(acetamiprid) into a 100 ml volumetric flask. Add 20 
ml of mobile phase, sonicate, and make up the volume 
upto the mark with acetonitrile. Pipette out 10 ml of 
this stock solution into a 100 ml volumetric flask. Add 
10 ml of the internal standard solution to it. Make up 
the volume up to the mark with mobile phase. Shake 
well to homogenize. 


A-5 ESTIMATION 


A-5.1 Inject 20 ul standard solutions until the area 
quotients of internal standard/standard of two 
successive chromatograms do not deviate from each 
other by more than 2 percent. Then use the following 
injection sequence: 


e CS, S, CS, S3 C $3... 
where 
C = standard solution; and 
S = sample solution (1, 2..., n). 


From the chromatograms of the standard solution, and 
sample solution, measure the peak areas of the active 
ingredient and the internal standard and calculate the 
percentage of the active ingredient as given in A-6.

ANNEX B 
[Table 1, SI No. (ii)] 
DETERMINATION OF pH 


B-1 PRINCIPLE 


The pH is determined using a pH meter having a range 
0 - 14 with a precision of 0.1 pH. 


B-2 APPARATUS 


B-2.1 pH Meter, direct reading, with glass electrode 
and a calomel reference electrode or any other suitable 
electrode. along with temperature compensation. 


B-2.2 Balance (Analytical), sensitive to 0.1 g. 
B-2.3 Buffer Tablets, tablets of pH 4.0, 7.0 and 9.2. 
B-2.4 Standard Glassware 

B-2.5 Wash Bottle, containing distilled water. 

B-3 PROCEDURE 

From the buffer tablets, prepare 4.0, 7.0 and 9.2 pH 


buffer solutions, following the prescribed instruction 
given with the tablets. Standardize the pH meter using 
the buffers as follows: 


Immerse the electrodes of the pH meter in 7.0 pH buffer 
solution and adjust the meter to read 7.0 pH. Remove 
the buffer solution from the electrodes, wash these with 
water and wipe the electrodes free from water. 


Replace with pH buffer solution 9.2 and adjust the 
meter to read 9.2 pH. Remove the buffer solution from 
the electrodes, wash these with water and wipe the 
electrodes free from water. Repeat the above procedure 
using 4.0 pH buffer solution. 


Weigh accurately about 10.0 g of the sample into a 
100 ml volumetric flask and make up the volume upto 
the mark with distilled water. Mix the sample 
thoroughly to get a uniform solution. Measure the pH 
of the solution. Report result to nearest 0.1 pH.
